title: Pullback to the Moving Averages
teaches: The pullback to the moving averages as we trade it: a leader in a stacked, rising trend drifts quietly onto a rising 10-day or 50-day, a session closes at or above the line, the buy is a market order as price trades over that session's high, the stop sits a few cents under the pullback low, a third comes off at 3R and 5R with the rest on the trail, and a loss taken at the stop is the system working.

questions.q: A pullback buy in this setup sits on which kind of line?
choices: A rising line in an uptrend
A falling line, to buy the bounce
A flat line inside a range
Any line the stock touched
questions.answer: A rising line in an uptrend
questions.why: A rising line in an uptrend. The 20 EMA and the 50-day must each be higher than 10 sessions ago.
questions.lesson_line: Buy the dip onto a line that is rising, never one that is flat or falling.

wrong.A falling line, to buy the bounce: A falling line is a downtrend. The card wants the line higher than 10 sessions ago.
wrong.A flat line inside a range: A flat line is a warning. The card says the line must be rising.
wrong.Any line the stock touched: Any line is how we end up buying a random average. The line must be rising.

questions.q: For a pullback buy, price is above the 200-day and the 20 EMA is above the 50 above the 200.
questions.why: True. Price over the 200-day, with the 20 EMA over the 50-day over the 200-day. No longs below the 200-day is a hard rule.
questions.lesson_line: Stacked averages first. Price, 20 EMA, 50-day, 200-day, in that order from the top.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: The stop sits a few ___ under the pullback low, not exactly on it.
questions.why: Cents. A few cents under the low, not exactly on it. Raschke put the protective stop at the newly formed swing low.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first: a few cents under the pullback low.

questions.q: The hold day is done and price trades over its high. How do we buy?
choices: A limit order well below the high
A market order, in regular hours
A stop-limit placed after the close
We wait for the next pullback
questions.answer: A market order, in regular hours
questions.why: A market order, in regular hours. Entries are market orders the moment the trigger trades.
questions.lesson_line: The trigger trades, you buy at market, and the stop goes in right away.

wrong.A limit order well below the high: A limit far below can sit unfilled while the stock leaves without us.
wrong.A stop-limit placed after the close: The rule is a market order the moment the trigger trades, in regular hours.
wrong.We wait for the next pullback: The trigger has traded. Waiting for another dip is not the plan.

questions.q: A pullback buy is for leaders: an RS rating of 80 or more, in a strong group.
questions.why: True. We buy leaders. An RS rating of 80 or more, in one of the strongest groups.
questions.lesson_line: Pullbacks are for leaders. A weak stock dipping to a line is not the same trade.

questions.q: How many entries and stops does one pullback trade have?
choices: One entry, then add on each dip
Two halves at two prices
One entry, one price, one stop
Three scale-ins under the line
questions.answer: One entry, one price, one stop
questions.why: One entry at one price, one stop. No adds and no second buy lower.
questions.lesson_line: One price, one stop, full size. No adding to a pullback buy.

wrong.One entry, then add on each dip: No adds. A second buy lower is ruled out.
wrong.Two halves at two prices: The full size goes in at one price with one stop.
wrong.Three scale-ins under the line: Scaling in is not ours. One price, one stop, no adding.

questions.q: On the card, what does a healthy pullback look like on volume?
choices: Heavy: above the 50-day average
Rising each day it falls
Volume does not matter at all
Quiet: below the 50-day average
questions.why: Quiet. The average volume over the pullback days sits below the 50-day average.
questions.lesson_line: Quiet volume on the dip is the picture. Heavy volume under the line is not.

wrong.Heavy: above the 50-day average: Heavy selling into the line is a warning, not a pullback.
wrong.Rising each day it falls: Volume rising on the pullback is a B- cue on our card.
wrong.Volume does not matter at all: It is a grade cue, and a heavy close under the line is an invalidation.

questions.q: A pullback low that dips 0.5 ATR under the line can still count as a touch.
questions.why: True. The touch is a low within 1 ATR under to 0.25 ATR over the line. So 0.5 ATR under is inside the range.
questions.lesson_line: The touch is a band around the line, not one exact price.

questions.q: How deep must the dip be to count as a pullback?
choices: Close 1 ATR under the 11-day high
A close 1% under the 11-day high
Down 25% from the 52-week high
Any red day at all counts as a dip
questions.why: A close at least 1 ATR under the highest high of the last 11 sessions.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the dip in ATR from the recent high. One ATR is the minimum.

wrong.A close 1% under the 11-day high: A percent can be tiny on a quiet stock. The card measures in ATR.
wrong.Down 25% from the 52-week high: That is far too deep. Within 25% of the high is the limit of the trend filter.
wrong.Any red day at all counts as a dip: One red day is not a pullback. The card wants a 1 ATR dip.

questions.q: How long does the pullback last, swing high to touch day?
choices: 1 session
2 to 8 sessions
10 to 15 sessions
30 or more sessions
questions.why: 2 to 8 sessions from the swing high to the touch day.
questions.lesson_line: Two to eight sessions of drift. A single day is a drop, a month is a base.

wrong.1 session: One day down is a sharp drop, not a drift.
wrong.10 to 15 sessions: That is longer than this card allows.
wrong.30 or more sessions: A month of drifting is a different pattern, not this pullback.

questions.q: A pullback can include one red day larger than 3 ATR and still be called orderly.
questions.why: False. Orderly means no single down day larger than 2 ATR in the pullback.
questions.lesson_line: Orderly means no single down day larger than 2 ATR.

questions.q: What makes a session the hold day?
choices: It trades the highest volume of the dip
It closes below the line by 1 ATR
Its close is at or above the line
It gaps down through the stop
questions.answer: Its close is at or above the line
questions.why: The touch day closes at or above the line. That close is the hold.
questions.lesson_line: A hold is a close at or above the line. Then wait for the trigger.

wrong.It trades the highest volume of the dip: Volume does not name the hold day. The close against the line does.
wrong.It closes below the line by 1 ATR: A close that far under is the line giving way, not holding.
wrong.It gaps down through the stop: That is a loss, not a hold.

questions.q: In an Orange market we take A+ setups only.
questions.why: True. Green is full risk, Yellow smaller and fewer, Orange A+ only, Red mostly cash and shorts.
questions.lesson_line: The market reading sets how much and which setups. Orange means A+ only.

questions.q: What is the minimum price and daily traded value?
choices: $5 and $1 million a day
$20 and $100 million a day
No minimum if RS is 90
$10 and $20 million a day
questions.why: $10 and $20 million a day. Only stocks at $10 or more that trade at least $20 million a day.
questions.lesson_line: Price $10 or more and $20 million or more traded a day. Thin names are not watched.

wrong.$5 and $1 million a day: That lets in thin stocks we do not even watch.
wrong.$20 and $100 million a day: That is stricter than the rule. The floor is $10 and $20 million a day.
wrong.No minimum if RS is 90: Strong RS does not remove the liquidity floor.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: A gap against the stop: the first ___-minute low is the new stop.
questions.why: 30. After a gap against the stop, the low of the first 30-minute bar is the new stop.
questions.lesson_line: A gap through the stop: the first 30-minute low decides.

questions.q: Bought at 31.80 with the stop at 30.67. Where is 3R?
questions.why: 35.19. One R is the buy minus the stop. Add three of those to the buy. YELP reached 3R the next day.
questions.lesson_line: Know your 3R before the open. The first third comes off there.

questions.q: Is today the hold day?
choices: No, the low must stay above the line
No, it needs a second close above
Yes, it closed at or above the line
questions.answer: Yes, it closed at or above the line
questions.why: Yes. The touch day closed at or above the line, which makes it the hold day. Now wait for the trigger.
questions.lesson_line: One close at or above the line is the hold. The buy comes next, on the trigger.

wrong.No, the low must stay above the line: The low may touch or dip a little. The close is what counts.
wrong.No, it needs a second close above: One close at or above the line is the hold.

questions.story: A leader drifts four quiet days onto its rising 10-day. Today the low touched the line and it closed above it.

questions.q: Bought at 31.80 with the stop at 30.67. How far under the buy is the stop, in percent?
questions.why: 3.6. The stop is well over our 3%, so size comes down.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the stop in percent. Over about 3% means a smaller size.

questions.q: A stock 30% under its 52-week high still passes the trend filter for a pullback buy.
questions.why: False. Price must be within 25% of its 52-week high on the hold day, and 30% is outside it.
questions.lesson_line: Stay within 25% of the 52-week high. A deeper hole is a recovery.

questions.q: What usually comes before a pullback worth buying?
choices: A long, flat sleep under the 200-day
A breakout, earnings gap, up-cycle
A month of falling on heavy volume
Nothing; any dip at all will work
questions.why: A breakout, an earnings gap or a new up-cycle within the last 3 months.
questions.lesson_line: A pullback needs something to pull back from: a breakout, a gap, a new up-cycle.

wrong.A long, flat sleep under the 200-day: A stock asleep under the 200-day is not a leader in an uptrend.
wrong.A month of falling on heavy volume: Heavy selling is distribution, not a leader's rest.
wrong.Nothing; any dip at all will work: A dip needs a run to dip from. Bonde: buy the first pullback after a major breakout.

questions.q: The trade reaches 3R. What does the plan do?
choices: Sell everything and lock the gain
Add to the position on strength
Sell a third, stop to breakeven
Do nothing until it reaches 5R
questions.answer: Sell a third, stop to breakeven
questions.why: Sell a third and move the stop to breakeven. The hard rule is a third at 3R, with breakeven between 2R and 5R.
questions.lesson_line: A third off at 3R, then the stop to breakeven.

wrong.Sell everything and lock the gain: The plan sells a third at 3R and lets the rest work.
wrong.Add to the position on strength: No adds. The plan trims here.
wrong.Do nothing until it reaches 5R: The hard rule is a third at 3R.

questions.q: A fast mover's last third is trailed under the 10-day and sold on a close below it.
questions.why: True. Trail the last third under the 10-day for fast movers, the 21-day for steadier ones, and sell on a close below it.
questions.lesson_line: Fast mover, 10-day trail. Steadier, 21-day. Sell on a close below.

questions.q: Do we buy the break?
choices: Yes, the chart looks very clean
Yes, but with half the size
No; a report is within 3 days
questions.answer: No; a report is within 3 days
questions.why: No. No new buys in the 3 days before an earnings report. Hold through one only if the trade is already up 5R.
questions.lesson_line: Three days before a report, no new buy. Check the date first.

wrong.Yes, the chart looks very clean: A good chart does not move the rule. No new buys in the 3 days before a report.
wrong.Yes, but with half the size: Half size does not fix it. The rule is no new buy inside the window.

questions.story: The hold day just printed. The stock reports earnings in 2 sessions. Tomorrow it may trade over today's high.

questions.q: The 52-week high is 300.00. The stock closed at 238.00 on the hold day. How far under the high, in percent?
questions.why: 20.7. That is inside the 25% limit, so the trend filter passes. It is one check of many, not a buy.
questions.lesson_line: Percent off the high is a quick filter. Under 25% passes it.

questions.q: Do you add at 186?
choices: No, one entry, one stop
Yes, a lower price lowers your average
Yes, but only half the size
questions.why: No. One entry at one price with one stop, no adds and no second buy lower. The first stop is the exit.
questions.lesson_line: Do not add on a dip. The first stop still decides.

wrong.Yes, a lower price lowers your average: Averaging down is not ours. The stop is the exit.

questions.story: You bought the 50-day hold at 190. The stock dips to 186 and holds the line again.

questions.q: The 50-day is 410.00 and ATR is 9.00. The day's low was 402.50. How many ATR under the line did it dip?
questions.why: 0.83. The low is 0.83 ATR under the line, inside the 1 ATR band, so it counts as a touch.
questions.lesson_line: Divide the dip under the line by ATR. Within 1 ATR is a touch.

questions.q: Wait for tomorrow's reclaim, or drop it?
choices: Wait; one close proves nothing
Drop it; that is distribution
Buy now to catch the low
questions.why: Drop it. A close under the line on more than 1.5 times the 50-day volume is distribution, not a pullback.
questions.lesson_line: Heavy volume under the line is selling. It is not a pullback to buy.

wrong.Wait; one close proves nothing: A close under the line on more than 1.5 times the 50-day volume is distribution.
wrong.Buy now to catch the low: Buying into heavy selling under the line is the mistake.

questions.story: On day five of a pullback, the stock closes under its 10-day on 2.3 times its 50-day average volume.

questions.q: If the honest stop is 3.6% wide, tighten it to 3% and keep the full size.
questions.why: False. Over about 3%, the size comes down so the account risk is unchanged. Never move the stop up to make it fit.
questions.lesson_line: A wide stop shrinks the size. It never gets tightened to fit.

questions.q: Which stop is the mistake on this setup?
choices: A few cents under the pullback low
A stop order placed with the broker
Line minus a cushion, at full size
Size cut down to fit a wider stop
questions.answer: Line minus a cushion, at full size
questions.why: The line minus a cushion, at full size. The stop gets far wider than 3% and the size stays the same.
questions.lesson_line: Stop under the pullback low. Not under the line minus a cushion.

wrong.A few cents under the pullback low: That is the plan. The stop sits a few cents under the low.
wrong.A stop order placed with the broker: A real stop order with the broker is required.
wrong.Size cut down to fit a wider stop: Cutting size to keep the same account risk is the plan.

questions.q: After the first third at 3R, the next third comes off at 5R.
questions.why: True. After the first third at 3R, another third at 5R, then trail the last third.
questions.lesson_line: A third at 3R, a third at 5R, and the last third rides the trail.

questions.q: A pullback that gaps 5% over the trigger price is still fine to buy at the open.
questions.why: False. Skip if the fill would be more than 4% above the trigger price. Chasing costs size, not risk.
questions.lesson_line: More than 4% past the trigger, skip it. No chasing.

questions.q: The trigger is 31.80. What is the highest fill we accept, with the 4% rule?
questions.why: 33.07. Four percent over 31.80. A fill above that is a chase and we skip it.
questions.lesson_line: Work out your chase ceiling before the open.

questions.q: Account 50,000, risk 1%. Buy 31.80, stop 30.67. How many shares, rounded down?
questions.why: 442. Shares are the account times the risk percent, divided by the stop distance, rounded down. The wider the stop, the fewer shares.
questions.lesson_line: The stop sets the size. Account times risk, divided by the stop distance.

questions.q: The dip averaged 1.2 million shares a day. The 50-day average is 2.0 million. What is the ratio?
questions.why: 0.6. The pullback ran at 0.6 times the 50-day average, under the 0.7 cue, so volume was quiet.
questions.lesson_line: Compare dip volume to the 50-day average. Under 0.7 is quiet.

questions.q: Price is 53.00. The 10-day average is 48.00. How far above it, in percent?
questions.why: 10.4. That is more than 10% above the 10-day average, so we skip the long as too stretched.
questions.lesson_line: Over 10% above the 10-day is too stretched to buy.

questions.q: Pullback or Remount?
choices: Remount; a line lost and retaken
Pullback; the 50-day held in the end
Pullback; big volume proves buyers
questions.answer: Remount; a line lost and retaken
questions.why: Remount. A pullback allows at most two closes under the line, the second reclaimed at once. Five or more is a line lost and retaken.
questions.lesson_line: Count the closes under the line. Two at most is a pullback.

wrong.Pullback; the 50-day held in the end: A pullback allows at most two closes under the line. Seven is a lost line.
wrong.Pullback; big volume proves buyers: Volume does not change the count of closes under the line.

questions.story: The stock closed under its 50-day for seven sessions in a row, one close more than 0.5 ATR under it. Today it closed back above it on big volume.

questions.q: Which card does this belong to?
choices: This card, the 10-day form
The 20 EMA Pullback card
The Remount card
questions.why: The 20 EMA Pullback card. A low that tags the 20 EMA and holds above the 50-day is that card in full.
questions.lesson_line: Name the line the low touched. The 20 EMA has its own card.

wrong.This card, the 10-day form: This card's trades are the 10-day in a fast leader and the 50-day. The 20 EMA has its own card.
wrong.The Remount card: Nothing was lost. The stock holds above its lines.

questions.story: A leader's low tags its 20 EMA and the stock holds above its 50-day. The 200-day sits far below.

questions.q: Pullback or Undercut and Rally?
choices: Pullback; the line held by the end
Neither; the line broke, so skip it
Undercut and Rally; buy the reclaim
questions.answer: Undercut and Rally; buy the reclaim
questions.why: Undercut and Rally. A buy taken as price trades back above a broken line is the Undercut and Rally, not a pullback.
questions.lesson_line: The buy names the setup. Over the hold day's high is a pullback.

wrong.Pullback; the line held by the end: A pullback buys over the hold day's high. This buy is the move back above a broken line.
wrong.Neither; the line broke, so skip it: The break and reclaim is a named setup of its own, the Undercut and Rally.

questions.story: At 10 am a leader's low breaks 1% under its 50-day. By noon price is back above the line, and you buy the move back through.

questions.q: Pullback or EMA Crossback?
choices: EMA Crossback; first test, new up-cycle
Pullback; any touch of the lines is one
Remount; the stock lost its lines
questions.answer: EMA Crossback; first test, new up-cycle
questions.why: EMA Crossback. After a Wedge Pop the test of the averages is the Crossback. A later touch of a line rising for months is the pullback.
questions.lesson_line: A test right after the new up-cycle is a Crossback. A later one is a pullback.

wrong.Pullback; any touch of the lines is one: A touch right after a new up-cycle is the Crossback. A later touch of a long-rising line is the pullback.
wrong.Remount; the stock lost its lines: It closed back above them. A remount is a line lost for five or more closes.

questions.story: Six sessions ago a stock closed back above its 9 and 20 EMA after a correction, a new up-cycle. Today it touches them for the first time.

questions.q: Pullback to the averages, or Bull Flag?
choices: Pullback; it touched the 10 EMA
Bull Flag; the 28% pole decides
Pullback; four days is too short
questions.why: Bull Flag. A bull flag needs a 20% or larger gain inside 20 sessions. A pullback needs no pole, only a rising line and a 1 ATR dip.
questions.lesson_line: A big, fast pole before a tight drift means a flag. No pole means a pullback.

wrong.Pullback; it touched the 10 EMA: A pullback needs no pole. A 28% gain in 9 sessions is a bull flag's pole.
wrong.Pullback; four days is too short: Length is not what decides it. The pole is.

questions.story: A stock gains 28% in 9 sessions, then drifts 4 tight days down onto its 10 EMA.

questions.q: Is this a pullback to buy?
choices: Yes, any touch of the 50-day works
Yes, if volume is quiet
No, the line has stopped rising
questions.answer: No, the line has stopped rising
questions.why: No. The line must be rising, higher than its value 10 sessions ago. A line that stops rising is out before entry.
questions.lesson_line: A flat or falling line is not support. Skip it.

wrong.Yes, any touch of the 50-day works: The line must be rising. Buying the touch just because it is the line is the mistake.
wrong.Yes, if volume is quiet: Quiet volume does not fix a falling line.

questions.story: A leader drifts down onto its 50-day. The 50-day is now lower than it was 10 sessions ago.

questions.q: Buy the break, or stay patient?
choices: Stay patient until it is back above
Buy; the stock is what matters
Buy half size to be safe
questions.answer: Stay patient until it is back above
questions.why: Stay patient. If the index loses its 20-day, wait until it is back above.
questions.lesson_line: A strong stock in a weak index still has to wait.

wrong.Buy; the stock is what matters: The card says to stay patient while the index is under its 20-day.
wrong.Buy half size to be safe: Half size is not in the plan. Patience is.

questions.story: Your leader passes every check. The index just closed under its 20-day for the first time in weeks.

questions.q: Which one is orderly?
choices: The two red bars; fast is clean
The six quiet days
Both are orderly
questions.why: The six quiet days. Orderly means no single down day larger than 2 ATR. The 2.5 ATR bars fail it.
questions.lesson_line: A sharp drop is not an orderly pullback. Slow and quiet is.

wrong.The two red bars; fast is clean: Orderly means no single down day larger than 2 ATR.
wrong.Both are orderly: A 2.5 ATR red bar breaks the 2 ATR limit.

questions.story: Two pullbacks reach a rising 50-day. One drifts six quiet days. The other drops on two days of 2.5 ATR red bars.

questions.q: What does that do to the grade and the size?
choices: Nothing; the grade and size stay
Tighten the stop to 3%
It grades down and the size shrinks
questions.answer: It grades down and the size shrinks
questions.why: It grades down and the size shrinks. A wide stop, over 3%, that forces a much smaller size is a B- cue.
questions.lesson_line: Wide stop, smaller size. Never a tighter stop to fit.

wrong.Nothing; the grade and size stay: A wide stop forces a much smaller size and is a B- cue.
wrong.Tighten the stop to 3%: Never tighten the stop to fit. Cut the size.

questions.story: A fast leader holds its 10-day. The pullback low sits 3.6% under your fill.

questions.q: Do you take it?
choices: No, Orange means A+ setups only
Yes, B setups are normal size
Yes, but with a tighter stop
questions.answer: No, Orange means A+ setups only
questions.why: No. Orange allows only A+ setups, and this is a B.
questions.lesson_line: The market reading comes before the chart. Orange is A+ only.

wrong.Yes, B setups are normal size: In Orange only A+ setups are taken.
wrong.Yes, but with a tighter stop: A tighter stop does not change the reading.

questions.story: A clean B-grade pullback shows up while the market reading is Orange.

questions.q: Which one is the cleaner pullback?
choices: The one with rising volume
The five days at 0.6x volume
They are equal
questions.why: The five days at 0.6x. Pullback days at or under about 0.7x the 50-day average are an A+ cue. Rising volume is a B- cue.
questions.lesson_line: Quiet is better than rising volume on the way down.

wrong.The one with rising volume: Volume rising on the pullback is a B- cue.
wrong.They are equal: The card grades quiet volume higher than rising volume.

questions.story: Two dips onto a rising 50-day. One runs five days at 0.6x the 50-day volume. The other has volume rising each day.

questions.q: Does the reversal help the grade?
choices: No, only volume grades a setup
No, a hammer means the line is weak
Yes, a tight reversal at the line helps
questions.answer: Yes, a tight reversal at the line helps
questions.why: Yes. A tight reversal at the line (hammer, inside day, undercut and reclaim) is an A+ cue. It keeps the stop at 3% or less.
questions.lesson_line: A tight reversal at the line keeps the stop small.

wrong.No, only volume grades a setup: The card names a tight reversal at the line as an A+ cue.
wrong.No, a hammer means the line is weak: A hammer at the line counts as a tight reversal, which our card lists as an A+ cue.

questions.story: A leader dips to its 10-day. The hold day is a tight reversal at the line, a hammer, and the stop is under 3%.

questions.q: Grading a pullback is a fixed checklist: tick every box and it is an A+.
questions.why: False. Grading a setup is discretionary and hard to define. The cues help, but no checklist makes it an A+.
questions.lesson_line: Grades are judgment with cues, not a checklist.

questions.q: What do we do about the 3.6% stop?
choices: Cut the size, keep the same risk
Move the stop up to 3% to fit
Skip it; the setup looks bad to me
questions.answer: Cut the size, keep the same risk
questions.why: Cut the size so the account risk stays the same. The stop is above our 3%, so size comes down.
questions.lesson_line: Wide stop on a fast leader: smaller size, same risk.

wrong.Move the stop up to 3% to fit: Never move the stop up to make it fit.
wrong.Skip it; the setup looks bad to me: The setup is fine. Only the size changes.

questions.story: YELP, 2013. A fast leader that rode its 10 EMA since February drifts four quiet days. You buy at 31.80 with the stop at 30.67.

questions.q: Which line was this pullback, and is it ours?
choices: The 200-day; it is the base
The 50-day; yes, the deeper form
The 10-day; this is a fast leader
questions.why: The 50-day, the deeper form. A mega cap's first test of the rising 50 SMA, six days on quiet volume, reached 3R in 10 sessions.
questions.lesson_line: The deeper pullback goes to the rising 50-day, in a leader.

wrong.The 200-day; it is the base: The 200-day is context, not the line this card buys.
wrong.The 10-day; this is a fast leader: The stock tested the 50-day, the deeper form, not the 10-day.

questions.story: CAT, 2025. A mega cap makes its first test of the rising 50 SMA after a long run. Six days down on quiet volume, then a tight hold.

questions.q: Does the dip pass the depth rule?
choices: No, it must be 2 ATR or more
No, six days is too long
Yes, just: it is at least 1 ATR
questions.answer: Yes, just: it is at least 1 ATR
questions.why: Yes, just. The close was at least 1 ATR under the 11-day high, and 1.01 ATR passes. The shallowest of the ten examples.
questions.lesson_line: One ATR is the line. MOH cleared it by a hair.

wrong.No, it must be 2 ATR or more: The rule is at least 1 ATR, not 2.
wrong.No, six days is too long: Two to eight sessions is the length rule, so six fits.

questions.story: MOH, 2018. Six days sideways on the lowest volume on the chart. The dip is 1.01 ATR deep.

questions.q: Does a three-day drop fit the length rule?
choices: Yes, 2 to 8 sessions covers it
No, it needs at least 5 sessions
No, a drop is never a pullback
questions.why: Yes. The pullback lasts 2 to 8 sessions, and three days fits. The stop was under 1%.
questions.lesson_line: Two to eight sessions, and three counts.

wrong.No, it needs at least 5 sessions: The rule is 2 to 8 sessions, so three fits.
wrong.No, a drop is never a pullback: A short, orderly drop onto a rising line fits if no day is over 2 ATR.

questions.story: BFAM, 2019. A three-day drop onto the rising 50 SMA in a steady grinder. The dip is 2.24 ATR deep.

questions.q: What does the third close under the line say?
choices: Buy; it dipped and came back
Skip it; it slices the line
Call it a Remount
questions.answer: Skip it; it slices the line
questions.why: Skip it. A third close under the line in the same pullback means the name keeps slicing the line. It is fewer than 5 closes, so not a Remount.
questions.lesson_line: Three closes under the line is a line sliced, not held.

wrong.Buy; it dipped and came back: A third close under the line in the same pullback is a skip.
wrong.Call it a Remount: Fewer than 5 closes under, so it is not a Remount either.

questions.story: ADI, 2023. In an 8-session pullback the stock closed under the moving average it was testing three times.

questions.q: Which check fails on this card?
choices: The line is rising
The distance from the high
The length: 2 to 8 sessions
questions.why: The length. The card allows 2 to 8 sessions and this took 10. On the 20 EMA Pullback card, a 10-session drift sits inside its window.
questions.lesson_line: Ten sessions is too long for this card. Judge it on the 20 EMA card.

wrong.The line is rising: That check passes here. Exactly one check fails, and it is the length.
wrong.The distance from the high: That check passes here. The length is the one that fails.

questions.story: META, 2026. A stock drifts 10 sessions from the swing high to its touch day. Every other check on the card passes.

questions.q: Which check fails?
choices: Within 25% of the 52-week high
The length of the dip
The line is rising
questions.why: Within 25% of the 52-week high. At 32.7% under it, this is a recovering stock's 10-day, not a leader's pullback.
questions.lesson_line: A stock far under its high is recovering, not leading.

wrong.The length of the dip: That check passes here. Exactly one check fails, and it is the distance from the high.
wrong.The line is rising: That check passes here. The distance from the 52-week high is what fails.

questions.story: AMD, 2019. A dip touches its 10-day on the hold day. The 52-week high is 34.14 and the close is 32.7% under it.

questions.q: Is this a pullback to buy?
choices: Yes, it is just testing the 50-day
No, a heavy close under the line
Yes, if it reclaims it tomorrow
questions.answer: No, a heavy close under the line
questions.why: No. A close under the line on more than 1.5 times the 50-day volume is distribution, not a pullback. This was 4.5 times.
questions.lesson_line: A heavy close under the line is selling. Skip it.

wrong.Yes, it is just testing the 50-day: A close under the line on more than 1.5 times the 50-day volume is distribution.
wrong.Yes, if it reclaims it tomorrow: The card drops it before entry. Heavy selling is not a pullback.

questions.story: TSM, 2025. A stock sits on its 50-day, then closes under it on 4.5 times its 50-day volume.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Move the stop down and wait it out
Buy again at once at the same price
Take it; re-enter on a new trigger
questions.answer: Take it; re-enter on a new trigger
questions.why: Take the loss and buy again only on a new trigger. The rule cannot see the market: the index was topping the same week.
questions.lesson_line: A planned loss is the system working. Re-enter only on a new trigger.

wrong.Move the stop down and wait it out: The stop only moves up, never down or wider.
wrong.Buy again at once at the same price: After a stop-out, buy again only if the setup triggers again, as a new trade.

questions.story: NVDA, April 2024 (prices split-adjusted). A clean pullback with stacked, rising averages. You bought at 90.10 with the stop at 87.57. Next day the stop is hit.

questions.q: Was the loss a rule break?
choices: No, the rules were followed
Yes, we should have waited
Yes, the stop was too tight
questions.why: No. The setup was followed and the line gave way, the card's failure mode. It never reached 3R in the window.
questions.lesson_line: A stop-out with every rule followed is a normal cost.

wrong.Yes, we should have waited: Every check passed. The line gave way, which the card names as the failure mode.
wrong.Yes, the stop was too tight: The stop sits under the pullback low. It was where the plan put it.

Only on a new trigger, as a new trade
No, never buy that name again
questions.answer: Only on a new trigger, as a new trade

questions.q: What do you do?

Move the stop to the gap day's low
Get out; past 2R the plan exits it
questions.answer: Get out; past 2R the plan exits it
questions.why: Get out. After a gap against the stop, the first 30-minute low is the new stop. If the first 30 minutes take the loss past 2R, get out.
questions.lesson_line: Gap through the stop: first 30 minutes decide, past 2R you are out.

wrong.Wait for a bounce back to the stop: The first 30 minutes decide, and past 2R we are out.
wrong.Move the stop to the gap day's low: The new stop is the first 30-minute low, and past 2R we exit.

questions.story: You hold a pullback buy. It gaps down through your stop. The first 30 minutes take the loss past 2R.

questions.q: Pullback to buy, or something else?
choices: A correction; the 50-day is flat
A pullback; it is inside 25% of the high
A pullback; a first touch is best
questions.why: A correction. A broken leader's first touch of the 50-day is a correction, not a pullback. The 50 was flat.
questions.lesson_line: First touch of a flat 50-day on a broken leader is not a pullback.

wrong.A pullback; it is inside 25% of the high: Inside 25% is only one check. The 50-day is flat.
wrong.A pullback; a first touch is best: A broken leader's first touch of the 50 is a correction.

questions.story: TSLA, 2024. A former leader is 20.6% off its high, with a flat 50 SMA. The pullback is 3.6 ATR deep and it touches the 50-day for the first time.

questions.q: What does the 5.9% stop mean for the trade?

Size down a lot, or skip
Move the stop up to 3%

questions.story: MU, 2026. A seven-day drift onto a rising line, 16.7% off its high. The stop is 5.9% under the buy.

questions.q: What does the plan say?

Add more; it is cheap
Sell it and free the money
questions.answer: Sell it and free the money

questions.lesson_line: Ten trading days under 1R, and the money moves on.

questions.story: You bought a pullback 10 trading days ago. The trade is still under 1R. The line has not broken.

Pass; the line is clearly falling
Pass; the dip is far too shallow
questions.answer: Take it; a calm dip held its line
questions.why: Take it. A leader that had ridden its 10 EMA since February drifted four quiet days onto the line. 3R came the next day.
questions.lesson_line: Rising line, quiet dip, a hold. That is the picture.

wrong.Pass; the line is clearly falling: Look again: the line is rising and price has ridden it.
wrong.Pass; the dip is far too shallow: The dip was 1.42 ATR, past the 1 ATR minimum.

choices: Take it; the dip touched the 10-day
Pass; the stock sits far under its high
Pass; the dip is too short
questions.answer: Pass; the stock sits far under its high
questions.why: Pass. It sat 32.7% under its 52-week high, outside the 25% limit. A recovering stock's 10-day, not a leader's pullback.
questions.lesson_line: A rising 10-day under a deep hole is a recovery, not a leader.

wrong.Take it; the dip touched the 10-day: A touch of the line is not enough. The stock is too far from its 52-week high.

questions.why: True. Picking the line after the fact is a listed mistake. Decide before the trade which line this stock respects.
questions.lesson_line: Pick the line before the trade. Never after the low shows where it stopped.

questions.q: How do you answer?

He is right; most pullbacks win
Skip the setup; 27.7% is too low

Sell it on the close under the 10-day
Add back what you sold

questions.lesson_line: The last third rides the trail and leaves on a close below it.

wrong.Hold until the 50-day breaks: For a fast mover the trail is the 10-day, sold on a close below it.
